headline: Designates new wilderness areas in central Idaho, adjusts Sawtooth National Recreation Area land rules, and transfers several parcels of federal land to Idaho counties and cities.
what_it_does: The law sets aside specified federal land in the Boulder-White Cloud Mountains as wilderness areas within the National Wilderness Preservation System. It keeps existing livestock grazing going where it already exists and lets agencies accept donated grazing leases in a designated grazing area. It also gives land without cost to Blaine, Custer, and Clayton-area local governments and the cities of Challis and Stanley for purposes such as a school bus turnaround, a park, a cemetery, a fire hall, a water tower, a wastewater plant, and about 20 workforce apartments.

who_it_affects.group: People who hike, camp, and visit the new wilderness areas
who_it_affects.how: The areas will be managed under wilderness rules, and commercial outfitting and guide services are allowed where needed for wilderness recreation.

who_it_affects.group: Ranchers with grazing permits on the affected land
who_it_affects.how: Existing grazing is allowed to continue, and leases or permits in the designated grazing area can be donated to the managing agency.
They may provide commercial services inside the new wilderness areas to the extent needed for recreational or other wilderness purposes.
The county receives up to one acre for a school bus turnaround at no cost, subject to terms the agency sets.

who_it_affects.group: Residents of Custer County and the cities of Mackay and Stanley
who_it_affects.how: The county receives land for a park, campground, fire hall, and waste transfer site, and the city of Stanley receives about four acres for workforce housing.
The city of Challis receives about 460 acres, and the city of Clayton receives land for a cemetery, park, water tower, wastewater facility, and fire hall.

who_it_affects.group: Workers in the City of Stanley
who_it_affects.how: The city may build up to 20 apartment units on the transferred parcel for people who work in the city or nearby, with building height and placement limits.
The law states that it does not reduce any Indian Tribe's treaty rights.
The federal agency must try to complete a land exchange for state land located inside the new wilderness boundaries.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on August 7, 2015, and the official summary does not list separate later effective dates for its provisions.
